summary.prose: S003 makes a dead or closed window unable to block the repository's chat queue. It fills the two lease stubs S001 left in the store (takeOver and reclaim) as guarded transactions, adds a guarded store method that marks a head message not delivered when its window is closed and a read of a window's presence row, and replaces the worker's ad-hoc recoverDeadLease with calls to these. A window that leaves no longer deletes its presence row, so a reload never looks like a closed window; the row ages out over PRESENCE_GRACE_MS. A lease reclaimed after a reload is followed by the worker until its CLI exits. The queue bound needs no new code: enqueue and resendFrom already refuse at 500 rows with a note, and finished rows are deleted at once.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A shared per-repository SQLite queue (node:sqlite, WAL, busy timeout) under ~/.insrc, written only in short IMMEDIATE transactions, with three tables: messages in queue order, a single-row repo lease with a heartbeat, and window presence keyed by a window key that survives a reload. A deps-injected queue worker in each window decides from the database alone when to take the lease, acknowledges the head message (queued -> processing) in the same transaction, and hands the turn to the existing turn lifecycle with its newest-wins rule removed; the per-session lease stays underneath as a guard against two CLI processes on one session. Takeover, not-delivered marking, retries and the flush are rules over these tables, and the outbox is a projection of them posted to the chat webview.

boundary.internal: The takeover rule (lease stale for LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS and both the holder window's process and the lease's CLI process gone), marking a processing message failed when its window died with no CLI left, re-attaching a turn whose CLI survived a reload (the reloaded window, same window key, reclaims the lease with reclaim() and follows the turn through the session's saved cursor), the not-delivered rule for a head message whose window is closed (no live presence past PRESENCE_GRACE_MS and its process gone), and the flush that keeps the stored records within QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The SQLite schema, the repo key and store location, the window key, the worker's polling cadence and timers, the turn runner and the chat host's change from starting turns to submitting them.
The outbox's markup, styles and live updates, and the handling of the outbox actions in the chat host.
The classification of a failed turn's error, the acted tracking, the retry schedule and the retrying row in the outbox.
Sending review-pane decisions through the queue, the removal of the review pane's waiting list, and keeping attachments of live messages.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — the outbox and a dead window

nonFunctional.performance: Enqueue, acknowledge and finish are each one IMMEDIATE transaction of a few rows, under 10 ms on a local disk; a window polls every 500 ms while its repository has live rows or it holds the lease, and every 5 s otherwise.
nonFunctional.security: The store holds message text and attachment paths in the user's home directory with the same permissions as the chat sessions under ~/.insrc; no new network surface.
nonFunctional.observability: Every acknowledgement, takeover, not-delivered marking, retry and refusal is logged through the chat's logger with the message key and window key.
nonFunctional.durability: WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL; done rows are deleted at once and the store never holds more than QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND live rows.

api.name: takeOver
api.signature: takeOver(claim: LeaseClaim, now: number, holderGone?: (lease: RepoLease) => boolean): boolean

parameters.name: now
parameters.purpose: the clock reading the staleness is measured against

parameters.name: holderGone
parameters.purpose: worker-supplied check that the holder window's process and the lease's CLI process are both gone, evaluated inside the transaction on the lease row it just read; optional and additive to the sc2 signature

returns.meaning: true when holderGone held and either the lease was stale for LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS, or the lease's windowKey equals the claim's (a reloaded window: the staleness wait is skipped, because the same window can no longer heartbeat it, and this is today's behaviour on every platform, including those with no process start times); its message was marked failed ('the window closed during the turn') and the lease row deleted in one transaction

errors.condition: the write waited past the busy timeout

preconditions: the lease is not held by this exact claim (windowKey and pid)
postconditions: on true no lease row remains and the message is failed with a resend
a lease of ANOTHER windowKey is taken only after LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS without a heartbeat

api.name: reclaim
api.signature: reclaim(claim: LeaseClaim, holderGone?: (lease: RepoLease) => boolean): boolean

parameters.name: claim
parameters.purpose: the reloaded window (same windowKey, new pid)

parameters.name: holderGone
parameters.purpose: true when the recorded holder pid is gone

returns.meaning: true when lease.windowKey equals claim.windowKey and the recorded holder is gone; pid and pidStartedAt are rewritten, seq and cliPid kept, heartbeat refreshed

errors.condition: the write waited past the busy timeout

preconditions: a lease row exists with the same windowKey
postconditions: on true the reloaded window holds the lease and can heartbeat it; the message is NOT failed
the worker uses reclaim only when the lease's CLI is still alive; a same-key lease whose CLI is gone goes to takeOver and is failed at once

api.name: markNotDeliveredIfHead

parameters.name: seq
parameters.purpose: the head message whose window is closed

returns.meaning: true when, re-reading the head inside the transaction (the store's LIVE_HEAD: the first row in seq order whose state is queued or retrying), the row's seq equals the given seq; the row is then not-delivered with error 'its window was closed' (a retrying head is marked too, so it cannot hold the queue); false when another window acknowledged, cancelled or finished it first or it is no longer the head

errors.condition: the write waited past the busy timeout

preconditions: the given seq is the head by LIVE_HEAD (state queued or retrying)
postconditions: on true the queue moves on to the next row; the message shows as not sent with a resend

api.name: windowAlive

returns.meaning: a presence row refreshed within PRESENCE_GRACE_MS exists

postconditions: existing behaviour; the worker does not call windowAlive alone to call a window closed: it combines presenceOf with isAlive (see the closed-window rule)

api.name: presenceOf

returns.meaning: the window's presence row (pid, pidStartedAt, heartbeatAt), or undefined when it has none

errors.condition: the read waited past the busy timeout

postconditions: a read only; no change to the store
new on sc2 (additive): the worker needs the presence pid, which windowAlive's boolean does not give

api.name: createChatQueueWorker

returns.meaning: the worker; its tick replaces recoverDeadLease. Closed-window rule: a window is closed only when its presence row exists with heartbeatAt older than PRESENCE_GRACE_MS AND isAlive(presence.pid, presence.pidStartedAt) is false, or it has no presence row AND the message is older than PRESENCE_GRACE_MS. Lease rule: a same-key lease whose holder pid is gone is reclaim()ed when its CLI is alive and takeOver()n at once when it is not; another window's lease is takeOver()n only after LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS. Reclaimed-lease rule: while it holds a reclaimed lease the worker heartbeats it and, each tick, checks isAlive(cliPid, cliStartedAt); when the CLI has exited it writes finish(seq, detached-ended) and releases the lease. dispose() no longer calls leave(): the window's presence row is left to age out

postconditions: a head whose window is closed no longer blocks the queue
a dead lease is freed without a check-then-act gap
a reload never leaves a gap in which the window looks closed: its presence row is still there, fresh within PRESENCE_GRACE_MS
a reclaimed turn's message is finished as detached-ended when its CLI exits, so it does not stay processing

dataModelChanges.details: No schema change. The not-delivered state and its error text already exist; S003 is the first writer of them outside tests. The bound counts failed and not-delivered rows as live rows.
reclaim rewrites pid and pid_started_at and refreshes heartbeat_at on the single lease row; takeOver deletes it. No column is added.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Adds markNotDeliveredIfHead to the store alongside the existing methods (additive); uses finish, enqueue and resendFrom unchanged. The bound is relied on as is.

Implements the takeOver and reclaim stubs S001 declared, adding an optional holderGone predicate argument (additive), and adds one read, presenceOf(windowKey), to sc2 (additive); uses windowAlive, lease, presence and release unchanged. takeOver skips the staleness wait for a lease of the claim's own windowKey.
Uses the existing failed and not-delivered outcomes; no new outcome kinds.

Changes the worker's tick: recoverDeadLease is removed and its tests moved onto reclaim, takeOver and the head rule; dispose() stops calling leave() so the presence row ages out instead of vanishing on a reload; the worker follows a reclaimed lease until its CLI exits and then finishes it as detached-ended. The display half of ac3 is existing S001 behaviour that this Story consumes unchanged: on every webview ready the chat host calls followLiveTurn (chat-panel.ts), which re-attaches the saved turn from the session file's cursor through turns.follow (turn-lifecycle.ts, follow()), and the new host takes ownership of the cursor once the old host's process is gone. So the reloaded chat shows the turn continuing without any change here; this Story only keeps the queue state (lease and message) consistent with it.

errorCases.scenario: Two windows both find the same stale lease and try to take it over
errorCases.detection: takeOver runs in one IMMEDIATE transaction that re-reads the lease row and compares heartbeat_at and seq before deleting; the second caller finds no row or a different seq
errorCases.response: the second call returns false and changes nothing
errorCases.userImpact: none; exactly one window moves the queue on

errorCases.scenario: The head message is marked not delivered while its window comes back
errorCases.detection: markNotDeliveredIfHead re-reads LIVE_HEAD in its transaction and updates only when the row is still the head (state queued or retrying) with the given seq; the window's acknowledge wins the race if it commits first
errorCases.response: markNotDeliveredIfHead returns false; the message runs normally

errorCases.scenario: The store is busy while the worker tries a takeover, reclaim or not-delivered marking
errorCases.detection: StoreBusy thrown by write(); the tick's try/catch logs it
errorCases.response: the rule is retried on the next poll; nothing is half done because each rule is one transaction
errorCases.userImpact: the dead window's lease is freed a poll later

errorCases.scenario: A dead holder's pid has been reused by an unrelated process
errorCases.detection: isAlive is called with pidStartedAt and cliStartedAt where they were recorded, so a reused pid with a different start time reads as gone; where start times are not recorded (platforms without /proc), the reused pid reads as alive
errorCases.response: pid reuse can only make a dead holder look alive, never a live holder look gone, so it delays recovery and never causes a wrong takeover. A live holder is never taken: another window's lease additionally requires heartbeat_at older than LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS, and a same-key lease is taken only when the holder pid is gone
errorCases.userImpact: at worst the dead holder's lease is held until the reused pid exits; no running turn is ever taken over (ac2)

errorCases.detection: liveCount() >= QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND in enqueue and resendFrom
errorCases.response: the message is refused with FULL_NOTE; nothing is deleted
errorCases.userImpact: the user sees the note in the chat and dismisses rows to continue

errorCases.scenario: A window reloads: it disposes its worker and creates a new one with the same windowKey while another window ticks
errorCases.detection: dispose() no longer deletes the presence row, so presenceOf(windowKey) still returns a row refreshed within PRESENCE_GRACE_MS when the other window checks; the closed-window rule needs a stale row AND a dead presence pid, or no row AND an old message
errorCases.response: the other window does not mark the reloading window's head message; the new worker refreshes the row on its first tick
errorCases.userImpact: none: the outbox shows the same messages after a reload

errorCases.scenario: A reload takes longer than PRESENCE_GRACE_MS to reach activation (a heavy workspace or slow extension start), so the old presence row goes stale with a dead pre-reload pid
errorCases.detection: the closed-window rule sees presenceOf(windowKey).heartbeatAt older than PRESENCE_GRACE_MS and isAlive(presence.pid, presence.pidStartedAt) false; it cannot tell this from a window that was closed
errorCases.response: the head message of that window is marked not-delivered with a resend; it is never lost and never run again by itself. This is the accepted trade-off of using the agreed PRESENCE_GRACE_MS (30 s) as the line between reloading and closed: a longer grace would hold the queue behind a genuinely closed window for longer
errorCases.userImpact: after an unusually slow reload the message shows as not sent with a resend; the user resends it with one action

edgeCases.input: the reloaded window (same windowKey, new pid) finds the old pid dead and the CLI dead
edgeCases.expected: takeOver succeeds at once (the lease is of the claim's own windowKey, on every platform): the message is marked failed with a resend and the lease freed, as recoverDeadLease does today

edgeCases.input: the reloaded window finds the old pid dead and the turn's CLI still alive
edgeCases.expected: reclaim re-homes the lease (pid rewritten, seq and cliPid kept) so the message is not failed; the worker heartbeats it, and when the CLI exits it finishes the message as detached-ended and releases the lease

edgeCases.input: another window's holder pid is dead and its CLI is dead but the heartbeat is only 2 minutes old
edgeCases.expected: no takeover until LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS has passed

edgeCases.input: a head message whose window has no presence row at all and which was queued more than PRESENCE_GRACE_MS ago
edgeCases.expected: treated as closed (the window never wrote presence, or it was pruned): not-delivered. A message queued less than PRESENCE_GRACE_MS ago is not judged yet

edgeCases.input: a head message whose window presence was refreshed 20 s ago (inside PRESENCE_GRACE_MS)
edgeCases.expected: not marked; the window is considered alive and takes it

edgeCases.input: a lease exists but its message row was dismissed or deleted
edgeCases.expected: takeOver deletes the lease and the failed-marking is a no-op on the missing row

edgeCases.input: the surviving CLI of a reclaimed lease exits while the reloaded window is running
edgeCases.expected: the worker's tick sees isAlive(cliPid, cliStartedAt) false, writes finish(seq, detached-ended) (the row is deleted; the turn is in the chat's transcript) and releases the lease, so the queue moves on

invariantsToPreserve.text: Ownership: a message is taken only by the window whose windowKey matches, and acknowledge takes the lease in the same transaction, so a message is never taken twice.
Every write is one short IMMEDIATE transaction; no rule spans two transactions.
The lease is held and heartbeated while the turn's CLI lives; it is released only when no CLI of that turn is running.
The worker decides from the database alone and holds no state that another window cannot see.

migration.stateBefore: takeOver and reclaim in chat-queue-store.ts return false unconditionally. The worker frees a dead lease with recoverDeadLease, which reads the lease and then calls finish() in a second transaction, and it never marks a head message whose window is closed, so that head blocks the queue. QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND already refuses at 500 rows.
migration.stateAfter: takeOver and reclaim are guarded single transactions; markNotDeliveredIfHead and presenceOf exist; dispose() leaves the presence row to age out; the worker tick calls reclaim, takeOver and markNotDeliveredIfHead instead of recoverDeadLease; a closed window's head message becomes not-delivered and the queue moves on. Schema version stays 2.

migrationSteps.action: Add presenceOf and markNotDeliveredIfHead to the store and implement takeOver and reclaim (additive; the stubs returned false so no caller depends on them)

Switch the worker tick from recoverDeadLease to the lease, closed-window and reclaimed-lease rules; stop calling leave() from dispose(); move the 97df9bf7 worker recovery test onto the new calls; invert the S001 dispose test's 'presence removed' assertion (chat-queue-worker.test.ts:151) to 'presence kept'
Hand check in two windows: reload mid-turn with the CLI alive, reload with queued messages in a second window ticking, and close a window with queued messages

migration.backwardCompat: No schema change and no change to any signature another story or the host calls: the new store methods and the optional holderGone argument are additive. Mixed versions, stated explicitly: a window still running the previous plugin keeps working against the same file, but its dispose() still deletes its presence row (leave()). When such a window is reloaded to take this update, a new-plugin window may see no presence row for it and, if its head message is older than PRESENCE_GRACE_MS, mark that message not-delivered once. That is accepted: the message is kept with a resend and nothing is lost; it happens only for the window that is being upgraded, once.

openQuestions: ac3, display half is carried by existing S001 code (followLiveTurn and turns.follow); it is not tested again here. The hand check in migration step 3 is the check that a reload with a live CLI shows the turn continuing; if that fails, it is an S001 defect to fix there, not a gap in this design.

HLD wording vs this LLD: the HLD boundary lists a flush that keeps stored records within QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND. This LLD builds no deleting flush: done rows are already deleted at finish, failed and not-delivered rows are only removed by the user, and a full queue refuses a new message with a note. Confirm no age-based purge of failed rows is wanted.
Epic constraints k1-k5 were not scored individually against the alternatives; none is contradicted.
The invariantsToPreserve cite HLD assumption ids (c11, c12, c13, c3) rather than analyze-bundle ids.
markNotDeliveredIfHead is a new store method not in the HLD sc1 sketch, and the optional holderGone argument deviates from the sc2 sketch signatures; both are additive.
sc2 additions: presenceOf(windowKey) is a new read on sc2 and takeOver skips the staleness wait for the claim's own windowKey; both are additive to the HLD sketch, and sc2 is owned by S001.

Decision for the owner: the line between a slow reload and a closed window is PRESENCE_GRACE_MS (30 s, the HLD's value). A reload slower than that marks the window's head message not delivered, with a resend, never lost. Using a longer grace for the head rule (for example LEASE_TAKEOVER_MS, 10 minutes) would avoid that but would hold the queue behind a genuinely closed window for up to that long. This LLD keeps the HLD's 30 s.
